uncited: Temporal Coherence and Caching accelerates volume rendering by exploiting the similarity between consecutive frames or adjacent rays, reducing redundant computation through spatial, temporal, or inter-ray state reuse.

It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [GL-NeRF](803-gl-nerf.md) and [Adaptive Sampling and Resolution](1412-adaptive-sampling-and-resolution.md) by prioritizing the reuse of previously computed geometric or color data (via buffers, caches, or reprojection) rather than solely adjusting sampling density or neural inference strategies.
The core mechanism shared by all children is the reduction of work units (samples, voxels, or pixels) processed per frame by leveraging correlation in time or space.
where $C_{acc}$ is the accumulated or cached value, and $\alpha$ is a blending or reuse factor determined by coherence metrics or guard checks.
